instruction: Hide notifications from appearing on the lock screen.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated Settings → Privacy → Screen, enabled Automatic Screen Lock toggle, and set Blank Screen Delay to 5 minutes in 9 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GNOME Settings panels, toggle switches on/off, use dropdown menus, understand privacy/screen lock settings.
metadata.task_rationale: Related task on the same Privacy → Screen settings panel. Requires toggling a different switch (Show Notifications on Lock Screen) which the model demonstrated capability for.
metadata.explanation: Task requires disabling lock screen notifications via Privacy → Screen settings. Evaluator checks gsettings show-in-lock-screen is false.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly runs 'gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.notifications show-in-lock-screen' which is the exact GNOME setting controlling lock screen notification visibility.
Expected value 'false\n' correctly matches the gsettings output when notifications are hidden from the lock screen.
exact_match metric correctly accesses rules['expected'] and compares it to the getter output, which is the proper data flow for type='rule' evaluators.
Single-requirement instruction ('hide notifications from lock screen') is fully covered by a single gsettings check — no missing verification steps.
